ROLE: Enter CLOSING so the session stops accepting protocol input but keeps its queued output, allowing a final PUBLISH fan-out and the responses already queued to reach the peer before the descriptor is closed.

STRUCT.NAME: struct session
STRUCT.ROLE: owner of the lifecycle state and queued output

STRUCT.NAME: struct byte_buf
STRUCT.ROLE: queued output that must be preserved

VAR.NAME: SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT
VAR.ROLE: may also enter CLOSING (EOF before CONNECT)

VAR.NAME: SESSION_CLOSING
VAR.ROLE: target state; repeated calls are no-ops

LOGIC.INPUT: s: borrowed session pointer, possibly NULL.
LOGIC.ACTION: 1) If s is NULL return. 2) If s->state == SESSION_CLOSED return (terminal: the descriptor is already closed and the queue was already discarded by the immediate path, so there is nothing left to flush). 3) If s->state == SESSION_CLOSING return (already flushing; repeated EOF/error notifications must not restart or clear anything). 4) For SESSION_AWAITING_CONNECT or SESSION_READY set s->state = SESSION_CLOSING. 5) Do NOT touch the output buffer: its length and bytes are exactly what the write pump must drain, and keeping them is what makes a response already queued for this peer survive a read-side EOF. Do not close the descriptor here either; the descriptor is closed by session_close_immediately() when the queue has drained (called by broker_reap) or when the write side fails, and by session_destroy() during shutdown. The receive buffer is likewise left alone; its remaining bytes were already processed by the caller (a trailing partial packet is simply never parsed again because the read pump only reads while the state is AWAITING_CONNECT or READY).
LOGIC.OUTPUT: No return value. A session in AWAITING_CONNECT or READY becomes CLOSING with its queued output untouched; a CLOSING or CLOSED session is unchanged.
INVARIANTS_USED: CLOSING means no further protocol input is accepted and the queue must drain
queued complete packets are preserved until written or until an immediate close
the readiness mask must keep EPOLLOUT set while queued output is non-empty, which is how a CLOSING session finishes without sending more data
LOGIC.PRECONDITION: s is NULL or points to a live session whose queued output may be empty or non-empty.
LOGIC.POSTCONDITION: s->state is SESSION_CLOSING when the session was AWAITING_CONNECT or READY; the descriptor, both buffers, the identifier and the subscriptions are unchanged.
LOGIC.THREAD_SAFETY: Not thread safe with respect to concurrent transitions on s.

runtime: client A CONNECT, then sends PUBLISH 't/x' payload 'p' immediately followed by shutdown(SHUT_WR)
